This note is to clarify how to handle a reconsideration.

If a motion to reconsider is called during a meeting then we handle it the usual way. But unusually, a motion to
reconsider can be moved up to 24 hours after the adjournment of the meeting. This option makes sense as
more information may come to light the following day and sometimes we need some time to reflect on votes
made in the pressure of a meeting.

How to handle a reconsideration motion moved *after* a meeting.


        ●​ Any supervisor who voted on the prevailing side of an issue can move to reconsider.
        ●​ The motion must be seconded, but the second can be any other supervisor however they voted,
         and including those not present at the meeting.
        ●​  Since there is a 24 hour deadline, the mover may directly contact any or all other supervisors to
          ask for a second - this is an administrative process so it falls outside the deliberative restrictions of
           the OMA.
        ●​ Once a second has agreed, the mover should inform the chairs and staff by email or text (or any
           other method with a timestamp) so we have a record that it was moved and seconded within 24
          hours after adjournment of the meeting where the item was considered.
        ●​ The mover and seconder may withdraw the motion to reconsider within that same 24-hour window.
         Once the 24-hour deadline is passed, the motion can not be withdrawn until it is being consdered
          as an item of business in a meeting.
        ●​   If the motion was proper, then a potential reconsideration of the matter will be added to the next
          scheduled meeting under Unfinished Business. For time-critical matters, a special meeting may be
             called.
        ●​ Once the motion to reconsider is accepted, further discussion of its substance would fall under the
       OMA so must be limited to no more than 2 supervisors unless we are in an open meeting.
        ●​ When the motion to reconsider comes to the board, the first vote is whether to uphold the original
           vote (NO) or reconsider the matter (and possibly revote) (YES). If the motion passes, then the item
         resumes as if it was just brought to the body (i.e. there is no motion on the table, amendments can
         be made, etc.)

I ESTABLISHMENT AND PURPOSE OF GIRDWOOD BOARD OF SUPERVISORS

II RULES OF PROCEDURE

Article 1 MEMBERSHIP

    A.​ GBOS consists of five Members, also referred to as Supervisors, elected in accordance to Anchorage
      code (Ref AMC 27.20.110).

    B.​ GBOS Members serve as both Public Servants and Elected Officials within the meaning of Anchorage
       Municipal Code. All procedures applicable to appointment, recall and removal of an Elected Official
       apply equally to Supervisors, unless Code provides specific exceptions. A non-exhaustive list follows:

       Resignation. A Supervisor may resign their seat in writing to the Chair(s) and/or to the Girdwood
       Service Area Manager.

      Vacancy by unexcused absences. A seat is declared vacant if the Supervisor fails to attend three
       consecutive regular or special meetings without providing an excuse, or fails to attend two-thirds of
       regular and special meetings in a twelve month period without excuse.

       Recall by voters. A Supervisor may be removed by the voters through a special recall election.

     Removal by Assembly. A Supervisor may be removed for a breach of the public trust through action
      by the Assembly.

      Appointment to vacant seats. When a seat is declared vacant, the Mayor will consult GBOS and
       appoint a qualified candidate, subject to confirmation by the Assembly.

    C.​ GBOS Procedure for appointment to a vacant seat.
     When a vacancy is established, a notice of vacancy shall be posted for a minimum of 14 days and
     maximum of 30 days, requesting nomination of qualified candidates and with a deadline for
       nominations at the end of the notice period.
       Within 7 days of the nomination deadline, GBOS will meet in an open meeting to consider the
      nominated candidates and perform due diligence on whether they are qualified and suitable.
       This meeting may only move into Executive Session upon a specific finding that information will be
       discussed which meets the necessary requirements for an Executive Session under the Alaska Open
      Meetings Act.
       At the meeting, GBOS may recommend a nominee to the Mayor for appointment.
            If no nominee is recommended by GBOS, one additional notice of vacancy may be posted. If the
      second nomination round fails to secure a GBOS recommendation, then GBOS will inform the Mayor
        that GBOS does not have a recommended appointee.

Article 2 MUNICIPAL CODE OF ETHICS

    A.​ As Elected Officials, Supervisors are subject to the Municipality of Anchorage’s Code of Ethics (Ref
    AMC 1.15).
      The Code of Ethics includes restrictions on the use of Municipal resources, limitations on accepting
         gifts and remuneration for representation, prior disclosure of interests in Municipal contracts, and public
       disclosure of potential conflicts of interests.

ARTICLE 3 OFFICERS AND AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

    A.​ A Chair or Co-Chairs. At the first GBOS meeting following the certification of the annual municipal
        election, GBOS will elect a Chair to serve a one year term. Alternatively, GBOS may appoint two
       co-chairs instead of one Chair.
      The duties of the Chair (or Co-Chairs) is to:
             a.​ Act as presiding officer at GBOS meetings
             b.​ Solicit agenda items from Members and GVSA staff
              c.​ Work with GVSA administrative staff to call meetings and publish meeting agendas and
              associated material
             d.​ Represent GBOS as a body unless GBOS delegates specific authority to a Supervisor with
               relevant responsibility.
             e.​ Execute documents requiring GBOS signature, or delegate signature to a Supervisor with the
               relevant responsibility.

    B.​ Vice Chair. GBOS does not appoint a Vice Chair.

    C.​ Each Supervisor has a specific area of responsibility to ‘oversee’, which roughly aligns to GVSA
       services. These roles may be adjusted from time-to-time, but are currently:
             a.​ Fire
             b.​ Housing and Economic Development
              c.​ Land Use
             d.​ Police, Roads and Utilities
             e.​ Recreation and Trails
       Supervisors choose their area of responsibility at the same meeting as the Chair is elected. In the case
      where more than one Supervisor chooses the same area, it is allocated by seniority, When supervisors
      have equivalent seniority, allocation is made by lot.

    D.​ Supervisors are expected to attend relevant Committee meetings in their area of responsibility, respond
        to community requests, liaise with the service provider and report at regular meetings if the service
       provider is unavailable.

ARTICLE 4 MEETINGS

    A.​ Potential conflicts of interest shall be disclosed by Supervisors before a topic is discussed. The Code of
       Ethics (AMC 1.15.060) details the procedure and requirements for disclosure. In general, potential
        conflicts should be disclosed where there is a reasonable concern that a potential conflict might arise.

<lots more to go here>

ARTICLE 5 VOTING

    A.​ An accurate roll call of Supervisors shall be taken at the start of each meeting, and a statement on the
       record shall be made whenever a Supervisor joins or leaves the meeting while it is in session.

    B.​ Unless a Supervisor is recused from an item due to the determination of a substantial conflict of
        interest, or is no longer present at the meeting, all Supervisors must participate in a vote in either the
        affirmative or negative.

C.​ Voting may be performed by consent or by roll call, such that the vote of each member can be
       determined from meeting minutes.

    D.​ A motion passes if a majority of the Supervisors voting cast a vote in favor, unless a higher threshold is
       required by code or Roberts Rules.

    E.​ In the case of the first tied vote on a question, any Supervisor may immediately call for a revote. On a
      second tied vote, or first tied vote if no revote was requested, the motion fails.

     F.​ Reconsideration. Any Supervisor voting with the prevailing side of a motion may call for a motion of
       reconsideration. This motion must be seconded by any Supervisor. If this motion is called before
       adjournment, the motion of reconsideration is taken up immediately as the next item of business.

    G.​ Reconsideration after meeting adjournment. A motion for final action may also be subject to a motion
        for reconsideration if it is called and seconded within 24 hours of the adjournment of the meeting in
      which the final action was taken. The motion must still be made by a Supervisor who voted for the
        prevailing side and seconded by any Supervisor. In these circumstances, informing Supervisors that a
       motion for reconsideration was called and soliciting a second for the motion is an administrative action
        for the purposes of the Alaskan Open Meetings Act.




ARTICLE 6 CORRESPONDENCE FROM GBOS

    A.​ Resolutions. A resolution is a formal statement of the will of the body, and can be either in support or
       opposition to a particular position or action. Resolutions are signed on behalf of the body by the Chair,
       Co-chairs or the Supervisor of a relevant area of responsibility.

    B.​ Letter of Non-Objection. A LONO is typically used for administrative action where the body does not
      have a strong stated opinion or is formally stating no concerns with a particular project or action.

    C.​ Other Correspondence. GBOS may also write letters requesting further information, outlining
        conditional or initial positions, sharing background information etc. <Approval?>

ARTICLE 7 BUDGET PROCESS

    A.​ GBOS shall approve a Girdwood Valley Service Area budget no later than the September regular
       meeting. The service area budget shall be transmitted as a recommendation to the Mayor.

    B.​ GBOS shall hold at least two work sessions to develop the budget during the three months prior to the
      September meeting.

Hi all,

Wanted to circle back on the ongoing discussion around GBOS procedures and how they align
with Anchorage municipal expectations. I took some time to do a line-by-line comparison
against AMC 2.30 and AMC 27.10.040, and here’s the bottom line:

GBOS procedures are materially consistent with Anchorage municipal expectations. No
substantive discrepancies were identified.

There are stylistic and structural differences, sure—but nothing that indicates a conflict with
code. I looked specifically at the areas of officer elections, meeting frequency, voting, special
meetings, public testimony, and code of conduct. Language and format vary, but the intent and
function are in alignment.

Just wanted to offer this up since I know we’ve had a few rounds of meetings without full
resolution, and feedback is due Monday. Happy to share the detailed notes if anyone wants
them.

Thanks,
Kellie
